hints.title: Sorted Sub-interval Identification
hints.text: Even after rotation, dividing the array at any midpoint leaves at least one of the two halves strictly sorted. How can you test if the target falls within the sorted half?

hints.title: Target Inclusion in Sorted Half
hints.text: If the left half is sorted (nums[left] <= nums[mid]), verify whether the target lies in [nums[left], nums[mid]). If yes, narrow left; otherwise search right. Apply symmetric logic if right is sorted.

hints.title: Sorted Half Branching Procedure
hints.text: Set left = 0 and right = len(nums) - 1. While left <= right, compute mid. If nums[mid] == target, return mid. If nums[left] <= nums[mid], check if nums[left] <= target < nums[mid]; set right = mid - 1 or left = mid + 1. Otherwise check if nums[mid] < target <= nums[right]. Return -1 if not found.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 5000)
complexity.notes: Single pass binary search halving the interval based on which half is sorted.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Linear scan takes O(N) time, violating the explicit O(log N) runtime requirement.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(log N) time and O(1) auxiliary space without finding the pivot index first.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correctly identifying which half is sorted with <=, boundary comparisons for target inclusion, and handling single-element or unrotated arrays.

solutions.approach: Direct Binary Search with Sorted Half Disambiguation
